text:
🇲🇽💉 <u>149 million vaccines in two years: Mexico's health balance</u>

At today's mañanera, Health Secretary Kershenobich said Mexico has applied more than 149 million vaccine doses in two years, and child vaccination coverage is now at 90% or higher. The Salud Casa por Casa program has made 24.8 million home visits. Specialty consultations are up 36% over 2024, and 332 billion pesos went into medicine purchases in 2025–2026, with clinics receiving 125% more units this year.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>One year after the Judicatura was abolished, the judiciary is cheaper and still running</u>

Lotería Nacional unveiled Sorteo Superior 2899, with 2.4 million tickets printed, to mark the first anniversary of the Órgano de Administración Judicial. The judicial reform created that body to replace the Consejo de la Judicatura Federal. It inherited a 14.466 billion peso deficit from the old Judicatura and closed that gap by the end of 2025. The federal judiciary now reports more than 4.7 billion pesos in savings. Its president, Néstor Vargas Solano, put it this way: "austerity will be the rule, not the exception."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Federal magistrate charged with aggravated rape, and his tribunal handed him back his seat</u>

Pedro Rodríguez Chandoquí, a magistrate on Mexico's Federal Administrative Justice Tribunal (TFJA), has been formally charged with aggravated rape of a young woman who was a law student at the time. She filed her complaint four years ago. On August 4, the TFJA's governing board voted 5-0 to reinstate him, and the criminal judge then used that reinstatement as the main argument for letting him face trial free. He only asked for a 30-day leave last week. Contralínea's Miguel Badillo: "justice is still slow and negligent."

🇲🇽🩺 <u>For the first time, Mexico is drinking less soda and smoking less</u>

Health Secretary David Kershenobich reported that soft drink consumption fell 2.2% and tobacco consumption fell 7.1% from January to May 2026. It's the first recorded drop for both. The government credits its junk-food ban in 84,000 public primary schools and medical checkups for nearly 11 million students.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>The airport that was never built is now a cornfield</u>

The land the old regime seized for Peña Nieto's Texcoco mega-airport is feeding people again. Campesinos from 13 lakeside towns have recovered more than 4,500 hectares and now grow mainly corn and beans, plus fava beans, squash and forage. In the Atenco ejido alone, about 1,000 of its 2,000-plus hectares were planted this year. Two decades ago, Atenco was beaten and jailed for refusing to sell.
banner: TEXCOCO: AIRPORT LAND NOW GROWS CORN
